# Cirth v0.16.0

Cirth 0.16.0 makes the framework easier to compose with an existing design
system and with third-party content. It adds an explicit cascade boundary, a
subtree opt-out, portable design-token exports and two native-first UI
patterns, while fixing visible shadow and overflow regressions.

## Breaking changes

Every stylesheet now emits its rules inside the single cascade layer `cirth`.
Unlayered application CSS therefore wins over Cirth regardless of specificity
or load order. This makes overrides simpler, but it also means CSS that used to
load before Cirth and lose may now win; in scoped builds, unlayered host-page
rules also win inside `.cirth`. Importing a Cirth file with
`@import … layer(cirth)` nests its own layer as `cirth.cirth`, and this release
does not define sublayers. Review the Upgrading guide before adopting this
version.

## New APIs

- Add `.no-cirth` to an element to suppress Cirth's component declarations on
  that element and its descendants. This is a cascade opt-out, not full CSS
  isolation: the global reset, theme, inherited values, layout, accessibility,
  reduced-motion and print rules still apply. Selectors outside the subtree can
  also continue to react to it through relationships such as `:has()` or
  sibling selectors.
- Class-based builds gain `fieldset.segmented`, a joined radio-group treatment
  that preserves native selection, keyboard behaviour, submission, focus and
  forced-colors support.
- Class-based builds gain `table.controls`, which lets form controls sit
  directly in table cells without the usual doubled padding and stacking
  margin.
- Source builds accept `npm run build -- --prefix "--acme-"` to replace the
  `--cirth-` custom-property namespace. The prefix must start with `--` and end
  with `-`; the published package, its default prefix and the `.cirth` scoping
  class are unchanged.
- The package exports W3C Design Tokens JSON for both colour schemes through
  `@cirthcss/cirth/tokens/light` and `@cirthcss/cirth/tokens/dark`. Direct
  relationships are preserved as aliases, derived colours include their
  resolved value and unsupported CSS values are listed rather than discarded.

## Fixes

- Dropdown and popover shadows render again: each shadow layer now resolves its
  own scheme-aware colour instead of placing complete shadow lists in
  `light-dark()`.
- `.overflow-auto` now contains absolutely positioned helpers such as
  `.sr-only`, preventing hidden table headers from widening narrow pages.
- Preset tokens now apply inside the `.cirth` wrapper of scoped builds.
